unlisted_practices: Establish a lifecycle governance framework (True Lifecycle Approach) for health care AI spanning R&D, market approval, and post-implementation deployment, with patient protections from medical law and bioethics embedded throughout.
Regulate AI at the research and development stage through guidelines and technical checklists that embed legal and ethical principles.
Have AI researchers document data limitations and biases, including under-represented groups, potential harms, and unremovable model limitations.
Establish an expert review and certification process for health care AI research, analogous to an IRB but focused on AI ethics and safety, that complements rather than replaces IRB review.
Give patients a structured appeals process with human expert review of important AI decisions.
Communicate to patients in a simple format their rights, duties, and redress pathways when AI is used in their care.
Require regulatory approval for AI medical devices before they go to market.
Require developers to set up training programs for clinicians using their AI products.
Widen regulatory scope from product-level to system-level approval covering workflow integration, hospital authorization, liability, insurance, and ongoing algorithm re-evaluation.

screen.reason: This is a legal and regulatory policy paper proposing a 'True Lifecycle Approach' framework for the governance and regulation of AI in health care.
